values: GAME CONTENT WORKBOOK — HOW TO USE THIS FILE
This workbook defines ALL swappable game content. The admin edits this file and re-imports it to update
the entire game world — no code changes required.
Master        - One row per movie. Links a Boss, Minion, and their associated gear/specials together.
Bosses        - Full stat block, phases, special attack/buff, drop table, resistances/weaknesses per boss.
Minions       - Full stat block and drop table per minion (simpler than bosses, no phases/specials).
Weapons       - All weapons in the game (player-equippable, including ones that double as boss/minion gear).
Armor         - All armor/outfits in the game, with resistance flags per damage type.
SpecialItems  - All unique special items (1 copy of each can exist in the game world at a time).
Classes       - Player class options and their starting stat bonuses.
RandomEvents  - The pool of good/bad random events and their effects.
Settings      - All tunable game constants (the central config, editable without touching code).
KEY RULES TO REMEMBER WHEN EDITING:
- Every 'Name' column must be UNIQUE within its sheet — this is how sheets cross-reference each other.
- Damage Types (used throughout): Blade, Blunt, Ballistic, Energy, Arcane, Explosive, Venom
- Boss/Buff Types (Special Buff column): AC_BONUS, DMG_REDUCTION, ATTACK_BONUS, CRIT_BONUS, RESISTANCE_TYPE, HP_RESTORE
- Weapon Type must be exactly: Melee  or  Ranged
- Resistance/Weakness columns use TRUE/FALSE (boolean), not text.
- All stat columns (STR/END/AGI/LCK/PER) are flat bonus integers added on top of base values.
- Drop Chance columns are decimals between 0 and 1 (e.g. 0.15 = 15%).
- Leave a special item's 'AssociatedTo' blank only if it is shop-only and has no boss/minion tie-in (rare).
- Each Boss must have exactly ONE Special Attack and ONE Special Buff defined on its row.
- Each Movie (Master sheet) should define exactly ONE Boss Special Item and ONE Minion Special Item.
DO NOT rename the sheet tabs themselves — the importer looks for these exact sheet names.
Column order does not matter, but column HEADER NAMES must match exactly (case-sensitive).
- Bosses sheet: added SpecialBuff_DamageType column (used only when SpecialBuff_Type = RESISTANCE_TYPE).
- Weapons & Armor sheets: added AssociatedTo column (informational link to a Boss/Minion; blank = generic shop item).
- DropChance on Weapons/Armor sheets applies ONLY to boss/minion defeat drop tables, not the daily Shop rotation.
- RESISTANCE_STACK_CAP renamed to RESISTANCE_STACK_MIN_DAMAGE_PERCENT for clarity (0.25 = quarter damage floor, the minimum % of damage that always gets through).
- Added TRICKLE_AP_AMOUNT / TRICKLE_AP_INTERVAL_HOURS: players now also receive +3 AP every 6 hours (03:00/09:00/15:00/21:00 UTC) on top of the midnight reset.
- Added END_HP_REGEN_DIVISOR: END now also contributes floor(END/2) to passive HP regen per AP spent, giving it a stronger sustain identity.
- Added BOSS_LEVEL_WARNING_THRESHOLD: players are warned (not blocked) before fighting a boss/minion 3+ levels above their own.

values: Massively muscular barbarian, long dark hair, minimal fur/leather armor, broadsword, weathered rugged features.
Chrome-and-black armored cyborg, visored helmet exposing only lower jaw, bulky mechanical frame, sidearm holstered in thigh.
Athletic woman, short practical dark hair, jumpsuit or utility gear, often paired with a pulse rifle or exosuit loader.
Tall, long dark hair, kilt/period Scottish Highlander attire in flashbacks or modern trenchcoat in present day, claymore sword.
Armored law-enforcement uniform, gold eagle shoulder pad, closed visored helmet (jaw and chin visible), badge on chest, sidearm 'Lawgiver.'
Black/dark grey armored batsuit, pointed-ear cowl covering upper face, flowing cape, utility belt.
Heavily muscular soldier, dark hair, camo/military fatigues, tactical gear, war paint in later scenes.
Athletic build, short dark hair, everyday clothing transitioning to rugged action wear, confused/determined expression.
Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country
Older Starfleet captain, greying hair, gold command-style uniform, confident authoritative bearing.
Muscular Spartan king, bearded, red cape, bronze helmet with horsehair crest, crimson cloak, minimal armor (cuirass and greaves), spear and shield.
Lean, muscular, cropped or tied-back dark hair, tank top and tactical pants, hardened intense expression.
The Lord of the Rings: The Two Towers
Rugged human ranger, long dark hair and stubble, weathered leather/ranger cloak, sword (Andúril).
Slim, black shoulder-length hair, black trench coat and sunglasses, minimalist dark attire.
Muscular Roman general/gladiator, short dark hair and beard, red officer's cloak in army scenes or gladiator armor/tunic in the arena.
Bearded, rugged, heavy winter/Antarctic expedition gear, flare gun or improvised weapon, weathered expression.
Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back
Young, sandy-blond hair, tan/beige Rebel flight suit or simple tunic, lightsaber.
Athletic, blond hair, all-American look, often in a red athletic/flight jacket.
Small-statured (Nelwyn), curly hair, simple rustic peasant/farmer clothing, earnest expression.
Teenage girl, curly reddish-brown hair, 1980s casual attire.
Athletic, dark tousled hair, digitized glowing-lined bodysuit (blue circuitry) when inside the computer world; casual clothes in the real world.
Rugged everyman, short dark hair, plaid shirt with sleeve torn off, chainsaw or bladed hand prosthetic, boomstick shotgun.
Bespectacled academic, tousled hair, casual/adventurer clothing layered with earth-tone jacket.
Youthful to middle-aged king, plain or ornate plate armor depending on era of story, wields the sword Excalibur.
Young, dark curly hair, lean build, blue-within-blue 'spice' eyes (later in story), form-fitting stillsuit attire on Arrakis.
Thulsa Doom's eyes burn with the power of Set — your limbs grow heavy and your will falters!
Thulsa Doom's robes seem to ripple like scales as dark power coils around him.
He was not a king. He was not a conqueror. He was a god — and gods do not bleed. Or so he claimed.
Bald, gaunt older man with a serpentine calm; wears dark hooded robes; long grey hair when unhooded; associated with a giant snake-head staff and cult iconography.
ED-209 locks on and opens fire with its twin autocannons — the room does not survive.
ED-209 recalibrates its threat matrix and raises its weapon systems to full combat readiness.
You have twenty seconds to comply. Nineteen. Eighteen...
Hulking bipedal robot, roughly 10 ft tall, boxy armored chassis, twin oversized cannon arms, single glowing sensor 'head,' clawed feet.
The Queen recoils from a wound, spattering searing acid blood in all directions!
The Queen's chitinous plates shift and harden, deflecting incoming strikes.
Twelve feet of chitinous nightmare — she is the mother of the hive, and she does not forgive intruders.
Massive black biomechanical insectoid, elongated ridged head-crest, secondary inner jaw, long segmented tail, large egg-sac abdomen when stationary.
The Kurgan lunges with terrifying speed, his broadsword aimed at your neck!
The Kurgan absorbs stolen Quickening energy — his strikes crackle with stolen immortal power.
He has killed two hundred and twelve immortals across four centuries. He is very good at it.
Towering, muscular, long stringy black hair, heavy black leather/spiked armor, guttural voice, broadsword.
Ma-Ma takes careful aim and fires a high-velocity round at point-blank range — no drama, no speech.
Ma-Ma floods the environment with Slo-Mo — your perception dilates, your reactions lag fatally behind.
She ran Peach Trees from the top floor with a scar on her face and a Slo-Mo empire below her. Until today.
Scarred face (slashed cheeks/mouth from acid), stringy dark hair, gaunt, dressed in utilitarian streetwear, cold expression.
The Joker produces a detonator with a grin — the explosion was always part of the plan.
The Joker shrugs off all strategy — his wild unpredictability becomes terrifyingly effective.
Some men just want to watch the world burn. He's already lit the match. He's just waiting for you to notice.
Green stringy hair, smeared white face paint, red scarred grin, purple coat and vest, disheveled/asymmetric makeup.
The Predator locks its plasma caster and fires a precision energy burst!
The Predator vanishes from visible light — only a faint shimmer betrays its position.
It has hunted across a hundred worlds. It is not afraid of you. It is barely even interested — yet.
Tall, muscular humanoid alien, dreadlock-like head appendages, mandibled face hidden under a mask, reptilian-textured skin, thermal-vision mask, wrist blade and shoulder cannon.
Cohaagen triggers a Mars atmosphere purge — the pressure drop is immediate and lethal!
Cohaagen invokes the full authority of the Mars Colony Corporation — his security detail absorbs the blow.
He controls the air on Mars. Every breath you take is his gift. He can take it back whenever he likes.
Middle-aged, stocky, balding/short grey hair, stern bureaucratic look, business/military attire.
To be or not to be — fire!
Chang declaims Shakespeare and triggers a cloaked torpedo barrage from point-blank range!
Chang's Bird-of-Prey disappears from sensors, striking from complete invisibility.
General Chang, eye-patch gleaming, quotes the Bard from the bridge of a cloaked Bird-of-Prey.
Klingon, one eye covered by an eyepatch, ridged forehead, goatee, imposing military bearing, Klingon uniform.
Xerxes raises his arms and calls upon the power of ten thousand gods — the very air shakes!
Xerxes is flanked by the Immortals — incoming strikes are deflected by his divine retinue.
He called himself a god-king. Three hundred Spartans had opinions about that. So do you.
Extremely tall, bald, heavily pierced and gold-adorned, elongated features, deep resonant presence, minimal jewelry-covered clothing.
The T-1000's arm morphs into a razor spike and thrusts with terrifying speed!
The T-1000 flows back together, its liquid metal body reknitting what should be fatal wounds.
It does not feel pain. It does not feel fear. It cannot be bargained with. It will not stop.
Slim build, short dark hair, LAPD uniform, expressionless face, liquid-metal chrome form when morphing.
Saruman's commanding voice resonates with dark authority, shaking your very resolve!
Saruman raises a hand wreathed in pale light — an invisible ward absorbs the strike.
At the pinnacle of Orthanc, robes shifting from white to every color of corruption, Saruman raises his staff.
Elderly, long white hair and beard, white robes, tall wooden staff, piercing eyes.
Mr. Anderson. Smith levels his weapon and empties an entire magazine in one fluid motion.
Smith adjusts his tie and moves faster than the eye can follow — every strike lands with eerie precision.
He straightens his tie. Puts on his glasses. Mr. Anderson. You can hear the contempt in every syllable.
Slim, close-cropped dark hair, black suit, sunglasses, earpiece, unnervingly flat expression.
Commodus calls upon his Praetorian Guard — a coordinated strike from multiple directions!
Commodus fights with the reckless fury of a man who has never once been told no.
He was not a man of honor. But he was emperor. And in the arena, that was enough.
Fair-haired, clean-cut, Roman toga/armor, youthful but calculating expression.
The Thing's body erupts in writhing tendrils and caustic biological matter!
The Thing reshapes its cellular structure — Venom damage barely registers against its alien biology.
It could be anyone. It could be you. In the frozen dark of Outpost 31, trust is a luxury nobody can afford.
Shape-shifting body-horror creature, grotesque and irregular in any given moment, tentacled/fanged when transformed, otherwise mimics human or dog form.
Vader extends a black-gloved hand — invisible force seizes your throat and lifts you from the ground!
Vader's connection to the dark side surges. His movements become terrifyingly deliberate.
The breathing comes first. Then the black armored silhouette steps forward, red blade igniting in the dark.
Tall black armored figure, full-face segmented mask/helmet, flowing black cape, mechanical breathing sound.
Ming channels contemptuous energy through his ring — you are beneath his notice, and it shows.
Ming raises a hand and the court closes ranks around him, shielding their emperor from harm.
He rules Mongo with a bored wave of the hand and a ring that has never known refusal. Today, someone refuses.
Angular shaved head with pointed brows, thin mustache/goatee, ornate high-collared robes.
Bavmorda channels the ancient dark power — the very air curdles around her incantation.
Dark magic gathers into a shielding tide around the Death Queen.
Queen of Nockmaar, sorceress without mercy — a prophecy names her doom, and she intends to correct it personally.
Older woman, pale, dark elaborate gothic robes and headdress, imperious bearing.
You Have No Power Over Me
The labyrinth itself twists to attack — walls, stairs, and shadow all obey the Goblin King.
Reality warps around Jareth — every strike lands somewhere he no longer is.
Goblin King, master of an ever-shifting maze — he offers your dreams in exchange for surrender. He is used to winning.
Androgynous, wild spiked blond hair, pale sharp features, tight fantasy-glam attire, cape.
The MCP disintegrates a chunk of the grid around you — programs don't survive contact with the void.
The MCP rewrites the local rules of combat in its own favor.
A rogue program that absorbed too much, too fast — it no longer takes orders from anyone. Least of all you.
Non-humanoid — a menacing glowing red geometric/triangular digital entity displayed on a large screen array.
Evil Ash commands the deadite horde to surge forward and overwhelm you.
A mass of grasping deadite bodies absorbs the blow meant for him.
A twisted reflection of a chainsaw hand and a boomstick — everything wrong wearing a familiar face.
Bruce-Campbell-styled but twisted/mocking expression, tattered medieval-ish attire, missing hand replaced with a hooked/bladed prosthetic in his deadite form.
Ra channels pure solar energy through his staff weapon — a false god's wrath is still wrath.
Ra draws on stolen technology dressed as godhood to knit his wounds shut.
He has worn a thousand faces and called himself a god in every one of them. Nobody has told him no in five thousand years.
Bald, androgynous, gold/metallic elaborate Egyptian-styled headdress and robes, glowing eyes when powered.
The ancient spell tears through your defenses like paper.
Morgana bends the sword's own stolen power against its rightful bearer.
Half-sister, sorceress, usurper — she learned every secret Merlin ever taught, and forgave him for none of it.
Dark haired, pale, elaborate black/dark sorceress robes, cold regal beauty.
Feyd's poisoned blade finds every gap in your defense — precise, patient, merciless.
Feyd fights with the reckless aggression of a man bred for the arena.
Groomed from birth to be perfect and merciless in equal measure — the Baron's favorite nephew, and his sharpest weapon.
Bald with pale/white powdered skin, dark makeup around the eyes, lean muscular build, close-set intense features; typically seen in ornate black Harkonnen arena armor.
Robed and chanting, eyes glazed with devotion — the Serpent God's will made flesh.
Robed cultist, shaved or hooded head, tribal tattoos, simple dark robes, curved dagger or short blade.
Cop-killer. Crime boss. Creep. Boddicker runs Old Detroit with a smirk and a splatter pattern.
Middle-aged, mustached, slicked dark hair, rugged criminal look, leather jacket over casual clothes.
A sleek killing machine — six limbs, elongated skull, inner jaw ready. No mercy.
Standard Xenomorph warrior — black biomechanical exoskeleton, elongated domed head, no visible eyes, segmented tail, inner extending jaw.
A mercenary from another century — skilled, ruthless, and unconcerned with your survival.
Generic period-dressed mercenary swordsman, plain practical clothing and leather, longsword.
Ma-Ma's enforcer in Peach Trees — street-smart, dangerous, and knows every floor of the block.
Muscular, bald or close-cropped, scarred, gang enforcer look, streetwear typical of the film's dystopian city.
He keeps count of every life he takes with a cut on his own skin. He is running out of room.
Gaunt, shaved head, self-inflicted tally-mark scars across neck/chest, plain prison/inmate attire, unsettlingly calm expression.
A younger Predator proving itself on the hunt — fast, relentless, dangerously unpredictable.
Tall muscular humanoid alien, dreadlocked head appendages, mandibled face under a masked helmet, reptilian-textured skin, wrist-mounted weaponry.
Cohaagen's chief enforcer on Mars — professional, relentless, and personally invested in your death.
Stocky, dark crew-cut, intense/aggressive expression, mercenary tactical attire.
A Vulcan who chose betrayal over peace. Logical, precise, and ice-cold about it.
Vulcan woman, sleek dark hair in a controlled style, pointed ears, calm composed features, Starfleet uniform.
The elite of Xerxes's army, face hidden behind a mask, trained to break kingdoms.
Masked warrior, ornate dark armor and cloth wrappings, curved blade, uniform faceless look among ranks.
Chrome skeleton, red eyes, no hesitation. A weapon that never tires and never stops.
Chrome metallic skeletal robot frame, glowing red photoreceptor eyes, exposed servos and hydraulics, humanoid but clearly mechanical.
Bred in the pits of Isengard, scarred by war — this Uruk-hai fears nothing.
Large muscular orc-like humanoid, pale/grey skin, black armor, tusked lower jaw, aggressive stance, heavy blade.
Smith's partner. Identical suit. Identical lack of mercy. Slightly less monologuing.
Slim, close-cropped dark hair, black suit, sunglasses, earpiece, expressionless — visually near-identical to the other Agents.
Undefeated. Handpicked by Commodus. Sent to the arena with hidden tigers — just to make it interesting.
Muscular, weathered gladiator, dreadlocked or braided hair, scarred, ornate gladiatorial armor and weapon of a champion fighter.
Something is wrong with their eyes. Something is wrong with the way they move. Run.
Ordinary Antarctic research-station crew member outwardly, but capable of grotesque transformation — distorted, fanged, tentacled body-horror form when revealed.
A white-armored soldier of the Galactic Empire — disciplined, ruthless, never alone.
Full white segmented armor, black bodysuit underneath, featureless helmet with black eye lenses and mouth vents, blaster rifle.
Winged and proud, sworn to Vultan's sky kingdom — he dives before you can raise your guard.
Winged warrior, muscular, bare-chested with leather flight harness, large feathered wings, hawk-styled helmet.
Armored in the Death Queen's colors, loyal past the point of reason.
Black armored soldier, closed dark helmet, uniform menacing look serving the film's dark queen.
Chaotic, cackling, and more dangerous in numbers than any single goblin has a right to be.
Squat grotesque goblin creature, warty textured skin, ragged makeshift armor, crude spear or weapon.
The MCP's enforcer program — efficient, loyal, and built to end fights quickly.
Red-and-black armored humanoid 'program,' angular geometric design, glowing red circuitry lines, commanding posture.
Risen from unhallowed ground, still wearing the clothes it was buried in. It remembers how to fight.
Reanimated skeletal/decayed warrior, tattered medieval rags and rusted armor, empty or glowing eye sockets.
Masked, disciplined, and utterly loyal to a god who has never once looked back at them.
Gold falcon-head helmet, ornate gold Egyptian-styled armor, staff weapon, upright ceremonial guard posture.
Faceless behind a closed helm, sworn to Morgana's cause — armored head to foot and built for a long fight.
Dark plate armor with spiked shoulder guards, closed helm, era-appropriate medieval knight silhouette in a menacing dark finish.
Conditioned from childhood on a brutal prison planet — the Emperor's elite, and they know it.
Elite black-armored soldier, closed dark helmet, imposing rigid posture, minimalist militaristic design.
Tall wooden staff topped with an ornate carved serpent/snake head, dark cult iconography.
Curved single-edged sword, simple wrapped hilt, cult-warrior styling.
Twin oversized automatic cannons integrated into the robot's forearms, boxy industrial design.
Large, chunky black automatic pistol with an extended magazine, aggressive angular silhouette.
The Queen's own bladed forelimbs — long curved black chitinous claws dripping corrosive acid.
Segmented biomechanical tail ending in a curved bony blade.
Massive heavy broadsword, worn dark blade, plain functional crossguard.
Standard period longsword, plain steel blade, leather-wrapped grip.
Pump-action shotgun, worn utilitarian finish, sawn-off or compact profile.
Crude street-made blade, wrapped handle, utilitarian and unpolished.
Plain fixed-blade knife, worn grip, used with unsettling casualness.
Simple fixed-blade hunting knife, plain handle.
Retractable triple blades mounted on a forearm gauntlet, metallic alien design.
Shoulder-mounted alien plasma cannon, triangular targeting array, glowing energy charge.
Compact futuristic sidearm pistol, sleek utilitarian design.
Standard semi-automatic sidearm, worn grip, mercenary styling.
Curved crescent-bladed melee weapon with multiple gripping points, Klingon metalwork.
Sleek Starfleet disruptor pistol, angular sci-fi design, glowing emitter.
Ornate curved ceremonial blade, gold-adorned hilt, exotic Persian styling.
Long thrusting spear with a leaf-shaped metal head, plain wooden shaft.
The T-1000's own forearm morphed into a long liquid-metal blade, seamless chrome surface.
Combat pump/semi-auto shotgun, folding stock, military-industrial black finish.
Tall carved wooden staff with an ornate crystal or carved head, wizardly design.
Heavy curved orc-forged blade, crude jagged edge, black iron fittings.
Large chrome/silver semi-automatic handgun, boxy heavy-frame design.
Standard black semi-automatic sidearm, visually near-identical to the other Agents' weapons.
Short Roman military sword, straight double-edged blade, ornate imperial hilt.
Heavy gladiatorial sword, weathered blade, championship-worn grip.
A grotesque transformed limb ending in claws/tendrils, organic body-horror design.

Long bronze-tipped spear, simple wooden shaft, Spartan military design.

Long single-handed sword with an ornate hilt bearing elven engravings, gleaming reforged blade.
Matched pair of black semi-automatic pistols, sleek minimalist design.
Roman gladius/spatha-style sword, functional battle-worn blade.
Pump-action shotgun, weathered Antarctic field wear.
Hilt with a blue energy blade, simple cylindrical metal grip.

Broad-bladed battle axe, wing/feather motif etched into the head.
Streamlined retro-futuristic ray-gun pistol, chrome finish.

Delicate glowing wand, ornate fairy-crafted design, radiant tip.

Crude wooden club, knobby and roughly hewn.

A projected beam of energy fired from the MCP's screen interface, geometric red digital styling.
Circular glowing red-edged disc, thrown like a weapon/boomerang, digital program design.

Corroded jagged sword wielded by the deadite version of Ash, twisted and menacing.
Curved rusted scythe blade on a worn wooden shaft.

Tall Egyptian-styled energy staff weapon, ornate gold head.

Dark ornate ceremonial blade used for sorcery, etched with occult markings.
Long jousting lance, dark iron tip, plain wooden shaft.
Legendary sword with an ornate cruciform hilt, gleaming blade, said to emit a distinctive ringing tone when drawn.
Slim curved dagger with a concealed venom reservoir, ornate Harkonnen design. Note: sourced from Dune: Part Two, since Feyd-Rautha does not appear in Dune (2021).

Curved milky-white blade made from a sandworm's tooth, ornate Fremen hilt.

Long dark crystalline blade with an irregular tapered edge, black-purple translucent material, glowing violet fissures, and a heavy angular grip formed from dark metallic fragments.

Plain dark hooded robe, simple cult markings, rope belt.
Boxy grey/steel armored robotic chassis, riveted industrial plating.
Worn leather jacket over casual streetwear, rugged criminal look.
Glossy black biomechanical exoskeleton plating, ridged and organic.

Crude heavy black iron plate armor, jagged and mass-produced looking.
Immaculate plain black suit, white shirt, dark tie — deliberately uniform and featureless.

Explosions are just scenery. When everyone else runs for cover, the Action Hero grabs the biggest weapon available and walks toward the problem.
Fast hands, questionable plans, and impeccable timing. The Gunslinger usually shoots first and worries about the odds afterward.
Tracks, movement, hidden threats — the Hunter notices what everyone else misses and prefers to see danger before danger sees them.
Bullets, blades, explosions, crashing vehicles — apparently these are inconveniences. The Juggernaut survives first and asks questions later.
Never the strongest person in the room, but suspiciously often the one who walks out with the credits, the treasure, and somebody else's spaceship.
Behind a scorched bulkhead you find a mercenary's forgotten credit pouch, still clipped shut and somehow untouched by the firefight.
A burst of pure action-hero adrenaline hits at exactly the right moment; suddenly every doorway looks breachable and every obstacle looks temporary.
A grease-stained field tech with the confidence of an OCP engineer tightens three bolts, reroutes one wire, and declares your equipment 'basically immortal.'
A dusty maintenance locker clicks open to reveal something useful wrapped in old emergency blankets, untouched since the last time the building became a war zone.
A nervous informant slides you a data chip, glances over both shoulders, and insists the credits attached to it were never there.
For a few impossible seconds the world stretches into slow motion: shell casings hang in the air, dust drifts like snow, and you have time to act.
A battered Imperial cargo crate lies split open beside the trail, its contents stamped, catalogued, and very clearly no longer under Imperial supervision.
A black glass sphere flickers in the darkness, showing distant towers, strange battlefields, and one object that seems to be waiting specifically for you.
A smiling stranger bumps your shoulder in a crowded passage. Three steps later, the stranger is gone and so are some of your credits.
A loose piece of wreckage comes out of nowhere and introduces itself directly to your ribs. The universe does not apologize.
A shower of sparks erupts from your equipment as one overworked component finally decides it has participated in enough adventures.
Your motion tracker chirps once. Then twice. By the time you turn around, something has already hit you and disappeared into the scenery.
A pair of corporate enforcers block the corridor, inspect your credit balance with great interest, and charge an extremely unofficial transit fee.
A tiny mechanical click comes from somewhere inside your gear. The next sound is considerably more expensive.
Hours of running, fighting, climbing, and being dramatically thrown through scenery finally catch up with you. Even heroes need an intermission.
A pale light crawls across the floor as if cast by a distant tower. Your limbs feel heavier, your reactions duller, and the effect refuses to leave before midnight.
A surge of barbarian fury rolls through your muscles. Every object nearby immediately begins to look like something that could be lifted, swung, or broken.
A hard, chitinous sensation creeps beneath your skin, as though some fragment of an alien hive has decided you are worth reinforcing for the day.
Three red targeting dots sweep across your chest and vanish. Instinct takes over; you start moving with the sharp, economical speed of a hunter.
A battered pair of dice tumbles from an abandoned satchel and lands perfectly. Somehow, every small coincidence starts breaking your way.
The surface of a dark seeing-stone clears for a heartbeat. Every doorway, movement, and hidden detail around you suddenly seems painfully obvious.
Blue-white energy crackles over your hands and shoulders, leaving the air smelling of ozone and making everyone else seem just a little slower.
An unseen force clamps down on your arms like an iron command from a distant wizard. Even simple movements feel like pushing against a locked door.
A single green droplet hisses against your gear before you wipe it away. The damage looks minor; the sick, burning weakness that follows is not.
The world becomes syrup-slow around you, except this time you are the one trapped inside it. Every movement arrives a fraction too late.
A door jams, a strap snaps, and something valuable rolls directly into a drain. Whatever cosmic force governs bad timing has noticed you personally.
A sudden blast leaves your ears ringing and the room tilted at an angle it definitely does not possess. Fine details refuse to stay in focus.
Mechanical breathing echoes from somewhere behind you. Nothing touches you, yet your body hesitates as if the corridor itself has ordered you to stop.
A battle-worn hero steps from the smoke, studies you for one silent moment, then tosses you something useful before disappearing toward an even bigger problem.

values: Palpatine unleashes a concentrated storm of dark-side energy across the battlefield.
The Emperor draws deeply on the dark side, making every attack faster and more precise.
The Emperor has stopped hiding behind armies and apprentices. This time, the full power of the dark side is aimed directly at you.
Elderly pale man with a deeply lined face, yellow eyes, thin white hair, and a black hooded robe with wide sleeves; carries a compact red-bladed lightsaber.
Dormammu tears open the Dark Dimension and floods the battlefield with hostile mystical energy.
Reality bends around Dormammu, absorbing attacks before they can fully reach him.
A ruler of an entire dimension does not consider this a battle. To Dormammu, it is an interruption.
Colossal humanoid figure with a broad muscular torso, dark segmented armor, massive shoulders, and a head formed from bright orange-red flame surrounding a shadowed face.
Sauron brings his massive mace down with enough force to scatter everything in its path.
The Dark Lord's armor and will harden together, turning aside attacks that would fell ordinary foes.
The eye, the armies, the towers — all of them were only extensions of one will. Now that will stands before you in armor.
Towering humanoid in jagged black plate armor with layered metal plates, spiked shoulders, clawed gauntlets, a tall many-pointed helmet, and an enormous black iron mace.
Smaug fills the battlefield with a sweeping blast of dragon fire.
Ancient scales lock together like armor plate, dulling even the strongest incoming blows.
The treasure beneath him is measured in kingdoms. The confidence above it has been accumulating for centuries.
Enormous red-brown dragon with a long serpentine neck and tail, broad leathery wings, overlapping armored scales, swept-back horns, heavy claws, and amber eyes.
HAL seizes control of the surrounding systems, turning machinery, power and environmental controls against you.
HAL predicts incoming actions and reroutes systems before attacks can reach critical components.
There is no anger in the voice. No panic. Only the calm certainty that your continued presence is a problem to be solved.
Black rectangular computer interface panel with a circular glass lens at its center, glowing red around a small yellow-orange inner light; surrounded by clean white spacecraft wall panels.
Kronos tears the battlefield apart in a catastrophic eruption of molten rock, debris and primordial force.
Ancient stone and molten armor harden around Kronos, absorbing punishment that would destroy lesser beings.
The earth does not shake because Kronos is approaching. The earth shakes because Kronos is awake.
Mountain-sized humanoid Titan composed of rough black volcanic rock, massive stone limbs, jagged ridges, and deep glowing orange cracks filled with molten material.
Stay Puft crashes forward with enormous weight, flattening everything in his path beneath soft-looking but devastating mass.
Supernatural energy rebuilds Stay Puft's damaged body, restoring great chunks of his marshmallow form.
He looks cheerful. He looks harmless. Then a thirty-story marshmallow foot comes down through the roof.
Gigantic rounded white humanoid mascot with smooth puffy limbs, a broad smiling face, black eyes, a white sailor cap with blue trim, blue neckerchief, and red neckerchief knot.
Megatron overcharges his fusion cannon and fires a massive blast capable of tearing through armor and fortifications.
Megatron's targeting systems and combat programming surge to maximum output, making every strike brutally efficient.
He has conquered worlds, crushed rivals and survived wars that erased civilizations. You are simply the next obstacle.
Massive silver-grey humanoid robot with angular metal armor, blocky limbs, mechanical joints, red eyes, dark metallic accents, and a large cylindrical fusion cannon mounted along one forearm.
The sandworm erupts from beneath the battlefield and surges forward with enough mass to swallow vehicles whole.
Layer upon layer of immense ringed hide absorbs impacts as the worm drives relentlessly forward.
The desert begins to move. Then the horizon opens into a mouth.
Colossal tan-brown segmented worm with thick ringed hide, a cylindrical body, rough leathery surface, and an enormous circular mouth lined with multiple rows of pale curved teeth.
Godzilla's dorsal plates ignite with blue-white energy before an overwhelming beam of atomic power tears across the battlefield.
Godzilla's immense regenerative durability and armored hide make conventional attacks seem almost meaningless.
Sirens, collapsing buildings, and a roar that seems to come from the planet itself announce the King of the Monsters.
Enormous charcoal-grey reptilian titan with rough pebbled scales, a broad muscular body, thick legs, long heavy tail, powerful jaws, small deep-set eyes, and rows of jagged dorsal plates.
Somehow your pile of questionable salvage always sounds priceless when you describe it.
These Aren't the Prices You're Looking For
A confident hand wave and questionable negotiation tactics make everything mysteriously cheaper.
When diplomacy fails, apparently the correct answer is to pick up something much heavier.
Long walks, impossible odds, and terrible planning have become part of your conditioning.
The currency keeps changing from universe to universe. Your ability to acquire it does not.
You have stopped treating the laws of motion as mandatory.
You notice the trap just early enough to feel smug about it.
Probability has filed several complaints about the way you play.
Other people's unattended belongings have developed an unfortunate habit of following you home.
By the time everyone else realizes there's a fight, you've already started it.
A few inspirational minutes of running, punching, and dramatic music replace years of actual training.
Years of genre awareness have finally become a practical combat skill.
If the explosion didn't solve the problem, the explosion probably wasn't large enough.
Your preferred solution now comes with warning labels and an alarming number of side effects.
Subtlety is what happens when you don't have a sufficiently heavy object.
The stun setting was clearly put there for people with less interesting problems.
You have developed a suspiciously cinematic talent for solving disagreements with sharp objects.
Against all reasonable expectations, additional bullets continue to improve the situation.
Ancient mystical power is much easier to understand when you point it directly at the problem.
Explosions, collapsing buildings, and suspiciously accurate gunfire all seem to miss the important parts.
You somehow squeeze considerably more action out of every turn than the laws of time intended.
You keep recovering from injuries that should really have ended the sequel.
One attack solved the problem. The second one is just good professional practice.
